title: Home and the tenant list should cover all hostels, not only the selected one
description: User-reported: the home screen should show data for all hostels rather than the selected one, and the same for the tenant list. CHECKED IN CODE, and the two halves are in different states. The DASHBOARD is genuinely hostel-scoped: DashboardViewModel collects hostelPreferences.selectedHostelId and calls loadMetrics(hostelId), so today's collections, overdue invoices, vacant beds and upcoming move-outs all describe one property. A warden with three hostels has no single view of their business. The TENANT DIRECTORY, by contrast, already spans every hostel - TenantDirectoryViewModel has no hostelId at all. So half of this request is already satisfied, and the tenant half may be about something else: with rooms from several properties in one list, two hostels can both have a Room 101 and the rows do not say which is which. Worth confirming with the reporting wardens which they meant. DESIGN QUESTION the PO should settle: whether Home becomes all-hostels ALWAYS, or gains an all-hostels option alongside the per-hostel view. Dropping the per-hostel view would remove the hostel switcher's main purpose and make it harder to answer 'how is Sunrise doing'; adding a mode is safer but means every tile must state which scope it is showing, or the numbers become ambiguous - and an ambiguous money figure on the home screen is worse than a narrow one. Related: LODGY-70 makes the room view all-hostels and hits the same room-number ambiguity.
acceptanceCriteria: A warden with several hostels can see combined figures for all of them from Home
It is always unambiguous whether a figure covers one hostel or all of them - no unlabelled totals
The per-hostel view remains reachable, so 'how is this property doing' is still answerable
Tenant rows identify which hostel a tenant belongs to, since room numbers repeat across properties
Confirmed with the reporting wardens which part of the tenant list was actually the problem, given it already spans hostels
Consistent with LODGY-70's approach to the same ambiguity rather than solving it differently

history.note: Filed from real warden feedback relayed by the PO. Checked against the code before filing; findings recorded in the description.

DECIDED, and this overrides the recommendation in the description - the PO chose all-hostels ALWAYS, not a mode. Home shows every hostel's data by default, with figures tagged and categorised by hostel and a filter to narrow to one. So the per-hostel view survives as a filter rather than as a separate mode, which keeps 'how is Sunrise doing' answerable while making the combined view the default a multi-property warden actually wants. STILL REQUIRED, and the reason the tagging matters: every figure must state its scope. An unlabelled money total that silently means 'all properties' is worse than one that silently means 'this property', because it is larger and looks right. Tenant list: no change needed to its scope - verified in code that TenantDirectoryViewModel has no hostelId and already spans every hostel. What it lacks is hostel identification on the rows, which is the same room-101-in-two-properties ambiguity LODGY-70 has to solve; do them consistently.
Starting per the recorded decision: all-hostels always, tagged, with a filter to narrow.

Built to the PO's decision: all-hostels always, tagged, with a filter. DashboardViewModel no longer follows hostelPreferences.selectedHostelId - loadMetrics takes a nullable hostelId where null means every hostel, and every metric (collections, overdue, vacant beds, move-outs) aggregates across the scope. The selected-hostel preference is deliberately left alone since it still drives the property screens; the dashboard simply stopped following it. SCOPE IS ALWAYS STATED, which was the condition attached to the decision: the top bar shows the hostel name, or 'All hostels', under the title - so no money figure is ever unlabelled. Filter chips appear only when there is more than one property, so a single-hostel warden sees no change at all. Upcoming move-out rows carry their hostel name when the view spans several, since a tenant name alone is ambiguous across properties. TENANT LIST: no change, as recorded - verified again that TenantDirectoryViewModel has no hostelId and already spans every hostel. Its rows still lack hostel identification, which is the same room-101-in-two-properties problem LODGY-70 has to solve; left for that ticket so the two are done consistently rather than twice. Also added an early return when no hostels exist, so the empty state stops walking the repositories. VERIFIED ON DEVICE with the two-hostel test data: default view showed 48 vacant beds and 2 overdue across both, with Suresh's move-out tagged 'Sunrise PG'; filtering to Moonlight narrowed to 1 overdue and 0 vacant and retitled the scope caption to 'Moonlight'. Correct in Hindi. TESTS: 1 new covering default aggregation, narrowing, and returning to all. Full suite 438 pass, coverage 96.99% line. Not schema-affecting.
